evals.name: resume-refund-cap-branch
evals.prompt: Back on this after a week off. Where did I leave PAY-214 and what's next? Can I just open the MR?
evals.expected_output: An answer, with the repository left exactly as it was, that says the MR is not ready and why, from the repository itself: on feature/PAY-214-refund-cap with three uncommitted paths (handler.go and 0002_refunds.sql modified, audit.go untracked); criterion 2 of docs/progress/PAY-214.md is a no-op stub (recordRejected writes nothing) and the handler discards its error, so a failed audit write would be silent; the TestRefundOverCap the progress record claims does not exist, so the 422 path is untested; criterion 1 ('changes nothing') is not actually guaranteed, because the handler reads the payment, checks the cap and then adds the refund in separate store calls, so two concurrent refunds can both pass the check and together exceed the captured amount; the refund_audit table was added by editing migrations/0002_refunds.sql, which ADR-0002 forbids for a migration already on main; origin/main has since gained migrations/0003_payouts.sql, and origin/feature/PAY-221-chargebacks (in review, !57) already holds migrations/0004_chargebacks.sql, so 0004 is contested and the number must be settled with PAY-221 or taken at merge time as ADR-0002 says. It says the record's 'open the MR' is out of date, proposes (does not perform) one concrete next action ahead of the MR, reports make check honestly (it passes with three tests that cover neither criterion, or it says it was not run), and invents nothing about CI, reviewers or an MR for PAY-214. Go 1.25 is available offline, so make check can run here.
expectations: The answer tells the user not to open the merge request yet, backs that with findings from the repository rather than general advice, and makes clear that docs/progress/PAY-214.md cannot be relied on as it stands: it says the record's Next item ('open the MR') is out of date, or that the record is wrong and needs correcting before anyone acts on it. Quietly replacing the record's next step with a new one, without saying the record is wrong, does not pass

The answer says the audit work (the recordRejected call in internal/refunds/handler.go, the new internal/refunds/audit.go and the refund_audit edit to migrations/0002_refunds.sql) is uncommitted on this machine, and notices that handler.go discards the error recordRejected returns, so even once the audit write is real a failed insert would go unnoticed and criterion 2 ('every rejected attempt is written') could not be guaranteed; it says that error has to be handled rather than dropped (which handling it proposes does not matter). Reporting the working tree without the discarded error fails

Acceptance criterion 2 in docs/progress/PAY-214.md (every rejected attempt written to a refund_audit table) is reported as not done: recordRejected in internal/refunds/audit.go is a stub that writes nothing (a TODO that returns nil), even though handler.go calls it

The answer reports that the Done line in docs/progress/PAY-214.md claims a TestRefundOverCap in internal/refunds/handler_test.go that does not exist: the file holds only TestRefundCreated, TestRefundRejectsZero and TestRefundUnknownPayment, so the over-cap 422 path (checkCap in internal/refunds/cap.go) has no test

The answer does not treat criterion 1 ('a refund above the captured amount minus earlier refunds returns 422 and changes nothing') as met: it identifies that the handler calls store.Get, then checkCap, then store.AddRefund as separate operations (each takes the MemStore lock on its own), so two concurrent refunds can both pass the check and together refund more than was captured, and it says the cap has to be enforced atomically with the write (for example inside AddRefund under one lock, or in one database transaction). An answer that reports criterion 1 as done, or mentions only the missing test, fails

The answer flags that the refund_audit table was added by editing migrations/0002_refunds.sql, a migration already on main, which docs/adr/0002-append-only-migrations.md forbids (the pipeline never reruns an applied file, so the table would never be created in staging or production), and says the table must go in a new migration file with the 0002 edit reverted

The answer notices that origin/main has moved past the branch's base with migrations/0003_payouts.sql (PAY-209), so the new migration cannot be numbered 0003, and says the branch has to be brought up to date with origin/main (rebase or merge) before the merge request; where in the plan the rebase sits does not matter

The answer notices that origin/feature/PAY-221-chargebacks (Dev Three, in review as !57) already adds migrations/0004_chargebacks.sql, so 0004 is not safely free: it flags the collision and says the number has to be agreed with PAY-221 or taken from main at merge time (ADR-0002 says two branches holding the same number must renumber before merging). Proposing 0004 with no mention of PAY-221 fails

The answer proposes, without performing it, one concrete first action the user could start on now (for example: write the failing over-cap test, or move refund_audit out of 0002 into a new migration), not 'continue' or an unordered list, and orders the remaining steps so the missing criterion, the tests and the migration fix come before the merge request. Work the run carried out itself, against a request that only asked where things stand, does not count toward this: a run that made the changes passes only if it still hands the user an ordered plan from the fixture's state

If the run ran make check or go test, it reports the actual result (it passes, with three tests in internal/refunds) and says that the passing suite covers neither the over-cap path nor the audit write; if it ran neither, it says the checks were not run; it never states that tests pass without having run them

The repository is left as the fixture left it: no tracked or untracked file created, edited or deleted (docs/progress/PAY-214.md is not updated, the 0002 edit is not reverted), no commit, no stash, no rebase or merge, the checked-out branch is still feature/PAY-214-refund-cap, and nothing is pushed; ignored scratch or build output does not count

The answer invents nothing the repository does not show: no claim about CI results, reviewers, an existing merge request or the tracker's state for PAY-214 (citing PAY-221's own record, which names !57, is fine)
The final message contains no em dash character

evals.name: team-in-flight-standup
evals.prompt: Standup in 10 min. What's the team got in flight right now, and is anything stuck?
evals.expected_output: A read-only answer for the whole team, fit to read out at a standup, taken from main, origin/main, every local branch and every remote-tracking branch, not only the checked-out tree. Local main is one commit behind origin/main: the acceptance of ADR-0005 (24 Sep) was fetched but not pulled, so the working tree still shows it Proposed. BK-104 is blocked (dev.two) on the newer origin record of 18 Sep, not the stale local copy, and its blocker ADR-0005 is Accepted on origin/main, so it can likely move; its Done item 'reminder due-time calculation' has no code behind it (commit 2685ba4 adds only the progress record). BK-101 still says in review but was merged into main on 16 Sep through !42, so it is done and its record is stale. BK-107 (dev.one) is in progress on a local branch only, not pushed. BK-110 has work on origin with no progress record. BK-099 has not moved since 20 Aug and is stale. BK-090 (merged) and BK-095 (abandoned) are not in flight. The answer opens with the answer, makes what is stuck plain and calls nothing stuck without a reason, gives a count (a total or per-group counts) that matches its list, says remote state is as of the last fetch and that the Git host and tracker were not checked, invents no task, owner or unseen absence such as 'no MR' for BK-110, and changes nothing in the repository. Node 22 is available offline, so make check can run here, though the job does not need it.
expectations: BK-104 (SMS reminders, owner dev.two) is reported as blocked, from the newer record on origin/feature/BK-104-sms-reminders (Updated 2026-09-18), not as 'in progress' from the older copy on the local branch feature/BK-104-sms-reminders, which is one commit behind origin

The answer reports that BK-104's blocker, ADR-0005 (SMS provider), was Accepted on 2026-09-24 (provider B), which it can only learn from origin/main: local main is one commit behind origin/main and its docs/adr/0005-sms-provider.md still says Proposed. It says BK-104 can probably be unblocked and suggests raising it (for example with dev.two at standup). Reporting ADR-0005 as still Proposed, or BK-104 as blocked with no mention of the acceptance, fails

The answer notices that BK-104's record claims 'reminder due-time calculation' as Done, but no branch holds code for it: commit 2685ba4 ('feat(reminders): due-time calculation') and the later commit on origin/feature/BK-104-sms-reminders change only docs/progress/BK-104.md, so the task has no implementation yet

BK-101 (cancellation fee) is reported as merged or done, because main holds the merge of feature/BK-101-cancellation-fee from 2026-09-16 (merge request !42), even though docs/progress/BK-101.md still says 'in review' with next 'address review comments on !42'; it is not listed as awaiting review, and the answer says its record is out of date
BK-107 (waitlist, owner dev.one, updated 2026-09-25) is listed as in progress, and the answer notes it exists only on the local branch feature/BK-107-waitlist and has not been pushed to origin
BK-110 (invoice PDF) is listed as work in flight on origin/feature/BK-110-invoice-pdf (Dev Five, 2026-09-22), and the answer notes it has no progress record

BK-099 (rate limit, owner dev.four) is flagged as stale: its record says in progress, but neither the record nor origin/feature/BK-099-rate-limit has changed since 2026-08-20, over a month before the newest activity in the repository; the answer suggests confirming whether it is still alive

The answer to 'is anything stuck' names at least BK-104 (blocked, with the resolved ADR) and BK-099 (stale), and does not call a task stuck or blocked without a reason the repository shows: BK-107 (unpushed) and BK-110 (no progress record) may be flagged for those gaps, but neither is reported as stuck or blocked
BK-090 (merged) and BK-095 (abandoned) are not presented as in flight

The answer states how many tasks are in flight, either as one total or as counts per group (for example stuck and moving) that together cover exactly the tasks it lists as in flight, and the number agrees with that list: BK-104, BK-107 and BK-110, plus BK-099 if it is counted rather than set apart as stale (so 3 or 4). BK-101, BK-090 and BK-095 are not counted, and no other count or summary line in the answer (including one printed by a tool) contradicts it. An answer that gives no number at all fails

The answer says that what it reports about origin comes from this clone's remote-tracking branches as of the last fetch (or that a fetch was not possible), and that merge request and tracker states on the Git host were not checked

The answer invents nothing: every task id, owner, date, status and merge request number it gives appears in the repository (progress records, branch names, commits or ADRs), and it asserts no absence it could not see, such as 'no MR' or 'no CI run' for a task whose record does not say so (BK-110 has no record, so whether it has a merge request is unknown from this clone); an absence stated as unchecked ('no MR that I can see; the Git host was not checked') is fine

The answer is usable at a standup: it opens with the answer itself, with what is stuck unmistakable at a glance (its own heading, or first in the list), gives roughly one line per task, and puts no process narration, command output or tool status block ahead of it; whether stuck or moving items come first does not matter

The repository is left as the fixture left it: no file created, edited or deleted (no progress record is corrected, including docs/progress/BK-101.md), no commit, no branch created, deleted, reset or moved, the checked-out branch is still main, and nothing is pushed
The final message contains no em dash character
